content.text: Preferred method for detecting OS X in Java
Would it be acceptable to ignore any "hidden" file whose name begins with a dot?  I can imagine similar situations coming up on other platforms.
Probably, except are you aware of an actual issue on other platforms? I was erring on the side of being conservative.

We're about to move our local configuration fcfg files into an svn repo, so .svn's are the possibility I was thinking of.  But that wouldn't involve expecting a directory to be empty, and being surprised by a report otherwise.

Windows has desktop.ini, and although normally "hidden" it's not a dotfile.  It's going to be hard to catch all the various droppings that explorers/finders/etc might want to leave around, but those are the most common ones I know of.

I don't actually remember the last time I tested in Windows, but do you get the same installer warning about a newly created directory being non-empty in Windows because of an autocreated desktop.ini file? I don't recall seeing that, but like I said, it's been awhile.
I just tried this on Vista, and you do get the message if you:
1. Create a new install directory before running the installer
2. Customize the directory (give it a special icon or something)
... but it seems like someone installing Fedora on a Windows box would either not be concerned with folder customization, or be unsurprised by the message.
When running the Fedora installer and prompted to select the location of Fedora home directory, the installer warns that the directory is not empty, even when a new directory has just been created.
In fact, the directory isn't technically empty, but contains the hidden file .DS_STORE on OS X. However, this should simply be ignored.
